items.title: Migrant regularization skews unemployment data but lifts pension ratio
items.body: Registered unemployment in August rose by 44,419 people, up 1.92%, after the June 30 regularization added claimants to SEPE. Social Security lost 162,840 contributors, while 337,917 regularized foreign workers were registered by August 31. The same wave lifted the contributor-to-pensioner ratio to 2.5, a 16-year high. More than 350,000 workers have entered formal jobs, strengthening pensions but straining employment services.

items.title: Government rules out further minimum wage rise in 2026
items.body: The government will not raise the minimum wage further in 2026, keeping it at €1,221 gross per month in 14 payments. The decision comes despite provisional August inflation of 4.3%, meaning nearly 2.5 million workers will lose purchasing power. The government cited the Middle East war as a contributing factor and rejected union demands for an additional increase. Minimum-wage earners will see rising prices outpace pay.

items.title: Government pays €90 million to regions applying housing law
items.body: The government will transfer €90 million to five autonomous communities that apply the housing law and rent controls. Catalonia will receive €59 million, Euskadi €15 million, Navarra €6.6 million, Galicia €5.1 million, and Asturias €2.9 million. The money is earmarked for public housing, rehabilitation, and land acquisition. This is the first payout to regions enforcing rent controls.

items.title: Protests and police report corner Sánchez over Ceuta crisis
items.body: Hundreds of thousands rallied in Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, Zaragoza, Sevilla and Bilbao over Ceuta after more than 70,000 people entered on July 30-31. A CENIF police report says Moroccan forces gave "active guidance" to migrants and that crossings were planned. Pedro Sánchez faces Congress on Thursday without allies; Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska demanded explanations from police director Francisco Pardo.

items.title: Madrid F1 rentals ask up to €17,703 for three days
items.body: Owners near Madrid's new Formula 1 circuit are charging up to €17,703 for three days during the Spanish Grand Prix, with some properties priced at almost €5,900 per night. A chalet in Valdebebas, 55 metres from the circuit, is listed at €17,703 for the weekend, while another villa is offered at €15,807. The event runs from September 11 to 14. Prices have climbed, with one property going from €14,050 to almost €16,000.

items.title: Renfe posts first annual profit since before the pandemic
items.body: Renfe recorded a net profit of €60.2 million in 2025, its first profitable fiscal year since 2019, after losses of €2.9 million in 2024. The rail operator transported 531.4 million passengers, and revenue rose 19% to €2 billion. High-speed and long-distance ticket sales increased 7.5% to €1,469 million. The turnaround could support better services and rail investment.

items.title: Organ donors get full pay during sick leave
items.body: Workers who donate organs or tissues while alive are now entitled to 100% of their salary during sick leave. The special temporary disability regime, created by Law 6/2024, applies to living donors. Spain performed more than 6,300 organ transplants in 2025, with more than 400 people donating while alive. The measure strengthens labor rights for living donors.

items.title: Government extends data center regulation comment deadline
items.body: The government has extended the public comment period for a draft decree tightening data center requirements to September 10 at 17:00. The draft would require data centers to obtain a "European card" and to cover 80% of their consumption with new renewables. Industry association SpainDC requested substantial changes. The regulation could affect tech investment and jobs but has limited direct impact on most residents.
